Calibrated synthetic BDHS data

Source: R/synthesize.R
bdhs_synthesize.Rd

Builds synthetic recode data with the structure of bdhs_simulate() whose weighted estimates reproduce the official DHS values of a curated set of indicators (bdhs_official()), nationally and by division, residence and (optionally) wealth quintile. Only published aggregates are used, never microdata, so the result can be shared, bundled with papers and used for teaching, testing and fully reproducible worked examples whose headline numbers match the DHS reports.

Usage

bdhs_synthesize(
  survey = 2022,
  recode = c("KR", "IR", "PR"),
  targets = NULL,
  margins = c("division", "residence"),
  scale = 1,
  seed = 1
)

Arguments

survey

A survey reference understood by bdhs_survey_id() (a DHS round, 1993-94 to 2022).

recode

"KR" (children), "IR" (women) or "PR" (household members).

targets

Indicator ids to calibrate (see Details). NULL uses every supported indicator of the recode with an official value in the round.

margins

Margins to calibrate in addition to the national value: any of "division", "residence" and "wealth". NULL or character() calibrates national values only.

scale

Sample size relative to the real survey (clusters are scaled; households per cluster are kept). Small values give fast, coarser data.

seed

Random seed. The global random number generator state is left untouched.

Value

A tibble like bdhs_simulate() output, with attributes bdhs_survey_id, bdhs_recode, bdhs_simulated = TRUE, bdhs_synthetic = TRUE, bdhs_targets (the official values used: one row per indicator, margin and category), bdhs_synthetic_design (seed, scale, clusters, households per cluster, reference indicator, and inconsistent_margins: published breakdowns that were not calibrated because their denominators do not add up to the national one) and bdhs_fidelity (the result of bdhs_synthetic_fidelity()).

Details

Supported targets (each depends on one source variable that the synthesiser controls):

  • KR: rh_del_facility (m15), rh_del_csection (m17), rh_anc_4plus (m14), ch_vac_bcg (h2), ch_vac_dpt3 (h3/h5/h7), ch_vac_measles (h9), ch_diarrhoea (h11). Vaccinations are not available for 2022 and caesarean section not for 1993-94. For 1993-94 the KR file is restricted to births in the last 3 years, as in the real file.

  • IR: fp_cpr_any, fp_cpr_modern (v312/v313), fp_unmet_total (v626a), ms_married_by_18 (v511, all-women denominator through awfactt), and nt_wm_thin (v445) on request.

  • PR: nt_stunting (hc70), nt_wasting (hc72), nt_underweight (hc71), nt_wm_thin (ha40), hh_electricity (hv206).

Official values use the indicator's reference period (by_variable_label, e.g. births in the last 3 years). Divisions are matched to the divisions as surveyed in the round (older rounds publish Dhaka and Rajshahi under "Dhaka before 2015" and "Rajshahi/Rangpur"). A margin without published values for every category is skipped for that indicator, and so is a margin whose published denominators do not add up (within 2%) to the national denominator, because it then refers to a different population than the national value (this happens for the 1996-97 and 1999-2000 child anthropometry by residence).

Method

  1. Sample design. The number of clusters is the real number of the round (from bdhs_surveys) times scale; households per cluster are chosen so the number of women approximates the real sample. Clusters are allocated to division x residence strata in proportion to the official unweighted denominators of a reference indicator (births in the last 3 years for KR, currently married women for IR, the de jure population for PR), with at least two PSUs per stratum. After simulation the weights are post-stratified so that the weighted reference population is distributed across strata as in the official weighted denominators (the joint division x residence table is the product of the published margins, which is the only information available from aggregates). Weights are normalised to the DHS convention (mean v005 = 1,000,000).

  2. Cell model. For every target indicator the probability in cell \(c\) (division x residence, x wealth quintile when requested) is \(p_c = \mathrm{logit}^{-1}(a + b_{div} + c_{res} [+ d_{wq}])\). The coefficients are fitted by iterative proportional fitting on the logit scale (logit raking) so that the weighted synthetic margins equal the official margins exactly, using the synthetic weighted denominators of each cell (the indicator's own universe function, including all-woman factors for all-women indicators).

  3. Deterministic assignment. Within each cell the eligible records are ordered by a key and the first \(k_c\) receive the outcome, with \(k_c\) chosen so that the weighted cell proportion is closest to \(p_c\); a greedy controlled-rounding step then moves the \(k_c\) by single records to minimise the squared deviations of all calibrated margins (national included). Results are therefore exact up to the granularity of single records, not subject to Monte Carlo noise. Keys combine a mild wealth gradient with random noise, except for anthropometric targets, where the record's own z-score or BMI is the key and the cell's distribution is shifted (location shift) so that its shape is kept.

  4. Coherence. Source variables are rewritten consistently: caesarean births are facility births, delivery assistance (m3*) follows the place of delivery, modern users are a subset of users, unmet need only occurs among non-users, method (v312), method type (v313) and need status (v626a) agree, and electricity is a household attribute.

What is and is not reproduced

Reproduced: the weighted value of every calibrated indicator nationally and for each calibrated margin (see bdhs_synthetic_fidelity()), typically within a few hundredths of a percentage point at scale = 1 (official values are rounded to 0.1). The national value is implied by the margins and the synthetic population shares; it can deviate slightly when an indicator's universe is distributed across divisions differently from the reference population.

Not reproduced: joint distributions beyond the additive logit model (e.g. urban Sylhet), associations between targets or with non-target variables (they follow the simple simulation model), every non-target variable, fertility and mortality rates, and standard errors (the design is realistic in size and structure but intra-cluster correlation is not calibrated, so SEs are only indicative). Calibration is done per recode: synthesised KR, IR and PR files share their structure but are not calibrated jointly, so linked values (e.g. a woman's BMI in IR and PR) can differ. The 2022 short-questionnaire design (sqtype) is not reproduced.

Synthetic data must never be used for substantive conclusions; they are for teaching, software testing and reproducible demonstrations.

See also

bdhs_synthetic_fidelity(), bdhs_simulate(), bdhs_official().

Examples

# \donttest{
kr <- bdhs_synthesize(2017, "KR", scale = 0.2)
bdhs_estimate(kr, "rh_del_csection", by = "v025")
#> # BDHS estimates: 1 indicator | BD2017DHS | 95% CI
#> # A tibble: 2 × 11
#>   survey_id indicator     label v025  estimate    se ci_low ci_high n_unweighted
#>   <chr>     <chr>         <chr> <fct>    <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>        <int>
#> 1 BD2017DHS rh_del_csect… Deli… urban     43.7  2.07   39.7    47.8          445
#> 2 BD2017DHS rh_del_csect… Deli… rural     28.7  1.80   25.3    32.4          710
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: n_weighted <dbl>, api_id <chr>
bdhs_official("RH_DELA_C_CSC", survey = 2017, characteristic = "Residence")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 13
#>   survey_id year_label indicator_id  indicator            characteristic_categ…¹
#>   <chr>     <chr>      <chr>         <chr>                <chr>                 
#> 1 BD2017DHS 2017-18    RH_DELA_C_CSC Delivery by cesarea… Residence             
#> 2 BD2017DHS 2017-18    RH_DELA_C_CSC Delivery by cesarea… Residence             
#> # ℹ abbreviated name: ¹​characteristic_category
#> # ℹ 8 more variables: characteristic_label <chr>, value <dbl>, ci_low <dbl>,
#> #   ci_high <dbl>, denom_weighted <dbl>, denom_unweighted <dbl>,
#> #   region_id <chr>, breakdown <chr>
bdhs_synthetic_fidelity(kr)
#> # A tibble: 77 × 9
#>    survey_id indicator       api_id  margin category official synthetic     diff
#>    <chr>     <chr>           <chr>   <chr>  <chr>       <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>
